items.title: Trump pauses sweeping Russia sanctions package; Zelenskyy urges support for the sanctions
items.summary: AP reports, via ABC News and KPBS, that President Trump signed an executive order on 17 October pausing a package of sanctions on Russia's economy, two days before the deadline set in the law, and told Congress the pause was in the national interest without giving details. Zelenskyy urged backers to defend the sanctions and said Russia had hit more than 15 energy sites across Ukraine. Sen. Richard Blumenthal criticised the pause. Zelenskyy also said the US is working on a possible meeting with him and Putin.
items.why: Sanctions and energy shocks feed straight into oil prices, supply chains and the cost of doing business for Indian companies that recruit on campus.
items.src: ABC News, KPBS (AP), The Washington Post

items.title: Kenya's Ebola cases rise to seven, including three health workers
items.summary: AP reports, via ABC News, that Kenya's Health Ministry confirmed four new Ebola cases on 17 October: three health workers who treated the first patient and a relative who had been in quarantine. Tests identified the Bundibugyo strain. The first patient died on 5 October after flying in from Congo. About 128 of roughly 130 contacts are traced and quarantined, and the ministry says there is no evidence of community transmission and the public risk is low.
items.why: Outbreak response is a live case in health-worker safety, crisis communication and duty of care for employers.

items.title: Japan's MMX Phobos sample-return mission is set to launch on 20 October
items.summary: Pre-launch coverage says JAXA plans liftoff on an H3 rocket from Tanegashima at 4:41 a.m. Japan time on 20 October, aiming to bring back at least 10 grams from Mars's moon Phobos, with Mars arrival in August 2027 and Earth return in 2031. The launch time can shift, and no source yet confirms liftoff.
items.why: Long-horizon, multi-country projects like this show how partners, budgets and public trust are managed over a decade.

items.title: At least 19 die in a crowd crush at a Durga Puja venue in Kolkata
items.summary: AP reports, via ABC News, that a crowd waiting outside a pandal pushed forward and fell after rain began on 17 October. At least 19 people died and about 25 were hurt. Officials detained festival organisers, and a special investigation team led by a high court judge will look into possible negligence. Al Jazeera's early report put the toll at 17, so figures are provisional.
items.why: Event safety, crowd management and organiser liability matter for anyone planning campaigns, activations or campus events.

items.title: India's current account deficit narrows to $5.2 billion in August
items.summary: Business Standard and other outlets report the RBI's preliminary data, released on 15 October: the August current account deficit was $5.2 billion, down from about $6.1 billion a year earlier, helped by a smaller goods trade gap and a larger services surplus. For April to August the deficit widened to $18.3 billion from $12.8 billion. Reports also cite a large balance of payments surplus driven by capital inflows; treat that figure as preliminary.
items.why: A narrower external gap supports the rupee and borrowing costs, which shape hiring budgets and ad spends across sectors.

items.title: Sensex rises 414 points on 16 October as IT stocks extend their rally
items.summary: Business Standard reports the Sensex gained for a second day, closing up 414 points, with the Nifty near 23,146 and the Nifty IT index up about 4%. Other coverage says IT stocks rose for a fifth straight session, lifted by Tech Mahindra's results. The Monday session has not been reported yet.
items.why: Market sentiment in IT and services is an early signal for campus hiring in the sector that recruits most MBAs.

items.title: NVIDIA's RTX Spark Windows laptops go on sale for local AI agents
items.summary: NVIDIA announced on 16 October that RTX Spark PCs are available from ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft and MSI. Each pairs a Blackwell RTX graphics chip with a Grace processor and up to 128GB of shared memory, aimed at running AI agents on the laptop itself. Prices start at $2,599, and compact desktops are due in November.
items.why: On-device AI changes what tools a marketer or HR team can run privately on their own laptops, without sending data to the cloud.

items.title: RTX Spark laptops start at $2,599 and pack up to 128GB of memory
items.summary: NVIDIA says the machines offer up to 128GB of unified memory and up to 1 petaflop of FP4 AI performance, according to its launch announcement.
items.why: Hardware prices set how quickly local AI tools reach ordinary workplaces.
